findings.title: Require manage scope for group creation
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE because hasPermission() grants access when any requested scope matches. Consequently, an administrator with only view permission on all Groups passes GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()'s requireManage() check and can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. Restrict this check to MANAGE so read-only group permissions cannot authorize writes.

findings.title: Build the user-search filter from actual group IDs
findings.body: This method returns authorization resource IDs, but its callers use the result as realm group IDs in UserModel.GROUPS. Granting view-members or manage-members on all Groups therefore adds the synthetic all-groups resource's UUID to the membership filter, causing user searches—including the brute-force users endpoint—to return no members. Individual group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() also have no Groups type, so this scan misses their grants and skips the intended database filtering before pagination. Enumerate or resolve actual GroupModel IDs, and handle all-groups grants explicitly, rather than using authorization resource IDs.

findings.title: Enable group-member creation authorization for FGAP V2
findings.body: The user-creation fallback still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, which is not enabled when V2 is selected. A delegated V2 administrator granted manage-members and manage-membership on a group, but not manage on all Users, therefore receives 403 when creating a user with that group in the representation. The new group permissions authorize managing existing members but cannot reach the checks intended to authorize creating members. Include V2 in this feature guard and test group-restricted user creation.
